note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes): Dysuria and urinary frequency for just under a week; burning/stinging pain on urination; aching lower abdominal pain worsened by urination; pink discoloration of urine noted today (possible hematuria); no fever, nausea, vomiting, or back/flank pain; irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with variable bowel habits; no other chronic conditions reported.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): No family history of bladder or kidney problems or other relevant chronic conditions reported.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Combined oral contraceptive pill (combined pill; dose/route/frequency not documented); medication for IBS (name uncertain, possibly for cramp relief; dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not currently sexually active beyond long-term boyfriend; uses combined oral contraceptive pill; no consistent condom use; last unprotected intercourse approximately 1–2 weeks ago; no vaginal discharge reported.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Occasional social alcohol consumption; first time smoked weed 1.5 weeks ago; no regular tobacco smoking; diet and physical activity status not recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Not recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors: Lives in university halls with a flatmate; family lives nearby and patient maintains contact; studying English at university and reports enjoyment of course; no financial stressors reported.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded; patient denies fever or systemic symptoms; clinician did not find examination concerning.  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated: Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant: Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy: Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated: Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood: Urine sample planned for microscopy and culture; results pending.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected: Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated: Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline: Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due: Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date: Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due: Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present: Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings: Patient presents with classic urinary tract infection (UTI) symptoms including dysuria, urinary frequency, lower abdominal aching pain worsened by urination, and new-onset pink urine suggesting hematuria; no systemic features such as fever, flank pain, or nausea/vomiting; history of IBS without new bowel symptoms; sexually active with unprotected intercourse increasing risk of STI; allergy to clindamycin documented; current medications include combined oral contraceptive pill and IBS medication.  
- Working diagnosis: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis), supported by clinical presentation and DDx ranking as high likelihood.  
- Relevant differentials consistent with transcript and DDx:  
  - Sexually transmitted infection (urethritis/cervicitis) – medium likelihood based on symptoms and sexual history but absence of discharge lowers probability.  
  - Urinary tract stone (nephrolithiasis or ureterolithiasis) – low likelihood due to absence of flank pain or colicky pain.  
  - Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome – low likelihood given acute onset and hematuria.  
  - Bladder or urethral neoplasm – low likelihood given young age and acute presentation.  
- Plan: Initiate empiric antibiotic therapy with choice between Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin (dose/route/frequency not documented); urine sample to be collected and sent for microscopy and culture to guide antibiotic selection; advise adequate hydration and pain management with Paracetamol; patient instructed to return if symptoms worsen or systemic signs develop (fever, back pain, vomiting); education on symptom monitoring provided.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Patient advised to maintain hydration and use Paracetamol for symptom relief; strongly advised against repeated cannabis use for general health; no documented education on chronic disease prevention.  
- Patient health goals and priorities: Not explicitly recorded.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Not recorded.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Follow-up planned if symptoms do not improve within one week after antibiotic course and urine culture results.

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Not recorded.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not recorded.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Urinary tract infection (cystitis)  
  Likelihood: High  
  Justification: Classic symptoms of dysuria, frequency, lower abdominal pain, and hematuria with no systemic features, consistent with uncomplicated cystitis.

- Sexually transmitted infection (urethritis/cervicitis)  
  Likelihood: Medium  
  Justification: History of recent unprotected sex and urinary symptoms may represent urethritis despite absence of discharge.

- Urinary tract stone (nephrolithiasis or ureterolithiasis)  
  Likelihood: Low  
  Justification: Hematuria and lower abdominal pain present but absence of flank pain, colicky pain, or systemic symptoms reduce likelihood.
